findings.title: Null pointer dereference when destinationCalendar is null or empty array
findings.body: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or an empty array `[]`, the destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined`. The subsequent access `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` will throw a TypeError at runtime. The old code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`), which safely returned `undefined`. The fix should use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Logic inversion: slug is now set when billing IS enabled instead of when it is NOT enabled
findings.body: The original code `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` spreads `slug` into the organization when team billing is disabled (so the slug is immediately available without payment). The new code `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` spreads `slug` when team billing IS enabled, which is the opposite behavior. This means organizations created without billing will no longer get a slug, and those with billing will get a slug immediately instead of using `requestedSlug` pending payment. This breaks the intended organization creation flow.

findings.title: Dead code in updateEvent fallback: searching for calendar by falsy externalCalendarId
findings.body: In `updateEvent`, when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else branch of the ternary), the code does `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. Since `externalCalendarId` is falsy at this point, this find will never match any calendar (no calendar has a null/undefined/empty externalId). The result is always `undefined`, making the fallback non-functional. The same pattern exists in `deleteEvent` at line 317.

findings.title: Team destination calendars silently dropped when organizer has no destination calendar
findings.body: When neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null`. The subsequent line `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` uses optional chaining, so when `destinationCalendar` is `null`, the push is silently skipped and all team members' destination calendars are lost. This means collective events where the organizer has no calendar integration but team members do will fail to create calendar events for those team members.

findings.title: Calendar interface requires credentialId but multiple implementations do not accept it
findings.body: The `Calendar` interface now declares `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)`, but `LarkCalendarService`, `Office365CalendarService`, and `BaseCalendarService` (CalDAV) all define `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` without the `credentialId` parameter. While TypeScript allows this (functions with fewer parameters are assignable to types expecting more), the `credentialId` is silently ignored by these implementations. If the intent is for all calendar services to use `credentialId` to select the correct destination calendar from the array, these services need to be updated.

findings.title: Shared mutable credential variable across loop iterations may use wrong credential
findings.body: In `updateAllCalendarEvents`, the variable `credential` is declared outside the for-loop (`let calendarReference: PartialReference[] | undefined = undefined, credential;`). Inside the loop, when `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials`, a DB fetch is attempted. If the DB fetch fails or returns null for one iteration, `credential` retains its value from the previous iteration, potentially causing the wrong credential to be used for a subsequent reference's `updateEvent` call.

findings.title: Inconsistent expected destinationCalendar values across webhook tests
findings.body: The BOOKING_CREATED test expects `destinationCalendar: null` (line 119) while the BOOKING_REJECTED test expects `destinationCalendar: []` (line 249). This inconsistency suggests different code paths produce different representations for 'no destination calendar'. Webhook consumers relying on a consistent shape will need to handle both `null` and `[]`, which is a potential source of confusion and downstream bugs.
